title: feat(spec)!: refuse a sealed object whose default chain column tenant_id cannot chain its rows
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao6bxiPKCvVuzoFTExumbxoz)_

Fixes #34352
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: updated here — `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` § Sealing and the case-16 expected output in `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` now say that a seal with no usable `tenant_id` (and no `chainField`) is refused at parse; surface extended by claim amendment 7044528745 (option A)

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：作者在校验或保存一个开启了防篡改封存、却没有可用组织列的审计对象时，会立刻收到拒绝和修改建议；以前它能保存成功，但运行时一行也不封存。
- 为什么做：属于审计账本防篡改这一组工作，补上上一轮只处理了“显式指定组织列”、没处理“默认组织列”的那一半。
- 出错会怎样：判断有误时，只有新写或重新保存的封存审计对象会被误拒；已经存好的定义启动时照常加载，撤回这次合并即可恢复。
- 要你做什么：这是一处收窄，并改了对外发布的技能说明，需要你审批后由席位落地。

## What changes

> **BREAKING** (accept-set narrowing, `@objectstack/spec` `minor`). FROM: `{ name: 'ai_audit_log', fields: { id, created_at, payload }, lifecycle: { class: 'audit', retention: { maxAge: '90d' }, seal: { valueFields: ['payload'] } } }` parsed on main, and the sealer then reported it at `error` and sealed none of its rows. TO: the same object is refused at `lifecycle.seal`: "`lifecycle.seal` names no `chainField`, so the sealer chains each row by the default chain column `tenant_id`, which is not a field of this object." Fix: declare a text or lookup `tenant_id`, or name the chain column, e.g. `seal: { valueFields: ['payload'], chainField: 'organization_id' }`.

- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: the `chainField` refinement now runs one judgement, `sealChainColumnFaults`, for a named `chainField` and for the default `tenant_id`. It reuses the predicates PR #34351 added (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`, `injectedSystemColumnDefs`, `nonTextChainColumnType`, `isSealLeafOrderColumn`, the `valueFields` check); nothing is copied. Named-`chainField` messages are byte-identical to main. When `chainField` is absent, `tenant_id` is refused when it is (a) not a field of the object (the registry injects `organization_id`, never `tenant_id`), (b) not one text on every store, or (c) listed in `valueFields`.
- **Path: `['lifecycle','seal']`**, not `['lifecycle','seal','chainField']`. The author wrote no `chainField`, so a path to it names no authored node. The seal block is what the author wrote, and naming a `chainField` is half of every fix. The message points at `organization_id` only where the registry injects it. On an object that opts out of the tenant column (`systemFields.tenant: false`, `tenancy.enabled: false`) it points at a declared column instead, because `organization_id` would itself be refused there.
- The sealer keeps its runtime report for definitions that skip the parse. `sealer.ts` changes one comment, which had become false.
- The fixture named by #34351's dev reports, `object-lifecycle-seal.test.ts`, gains a `tenant_id`. The inverse pin in `object-lifecycle-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts` (old line 60) now declares `tenant_id`.
- Docs: `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` § Sealed audit objects, the `chainField` `.describe`, and the regenerated `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`.
- ADR-0087: semantic entry `seal-default-chain-column-refused`, and the changeset marker `registered seal-default-chain-column-refused`. The gate refuses `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` on a `narrowed` changeset.
- `docs/adr/**` is untouched (claim amendments 7044528745 and 4). ADR-0154's 2026-11-16 note ("The default `tenant_id`, when `chainField` is absent, is not judged at authoring; that half is #34352") is carried to the weekly "ADR revisions" card in the round this PR merges, per claim amendment 4.
- Patch round 1 (L1 7048125406, L2 7048183393), prose and pins only:
  - the changeset and the semantic entry now give the run-time history for each case: (a) reported at `error`, nothing sealed; (b) some or all rows sealed into the deployment chain with no report; (c) sealed per organization, with the committed value in clear as the chain. The fix line and the entry's `acceptanceCriteria` (as corrected in patch round 2, L2 M1 7049260981) say that removing `tenant_id` from `valueFields` keeps every chain and verifies ok, and that only a fix changing a row's chain value (case (b), or a different `chainField`) re-seals the last sealed window, reads `listed_twice`, and reads late and unsealed under `--org`;
  - `ObjectSchema.create()` and `defineStack()` are named as doors and pinned;
  - the `objectExtensions` false refusal is disclosed in the `sealChainColumnFaults` docblock, the changeset and the entry.

## Tests

- New `packages/spec/src/data/object-lifecycle-seal-default-chain-column-34352.test.ts`, 20 tests. Refusal pins assert code, path and the first sentence of the message:
  - (a) no `tenant_id`, plus two tenant opt-outs;
  - (b) six non-text `tenant_id` types;
  - (c) `tenant_id` listed in `valueFields`.
  CONTROLS: a text or lookup `tenant_id`; a `chainField` naming a declared field, or `organization_id`; a named `chainField` beside a number `tenant_id`. Door pins: `ObjectSchema.create()` (the located issue), `defineStack()` (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` plus the located issue), `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` (`os validate` / `os build`, also with a `tenant_id` only from `objectExtensions`) and `getMetadataTypeSchema('object')` (the save door).
- Narrowing size, measured: the base copies of the two old seal test files fail 18 tests under the new rule. 17 come from `object-lifecycle-seal.test.ts`'s no-`tenant_id` fixture and 1 from the 34164 inverse pin, all case (a).

<details><summary>Suite readings (os-verify-lock)</summary>

- spec, on 2cd55da594 (merged main): typecheck exit 0; Test Files 867 passed (867), Tests 27815 passed, 1 todo. VERDICT command-exit 0.
- plugin-audit, on 1ce3bc8342, after the closure build: typecheck exit 0; Test Files 103 passed (103), Tests 1729 passed. VERDICT command-exit 0. Its only change is the comment.
- spec `src/migrations`, after `gen:migration-registry`: Test Files 5 passed, Tests 198 passed.
- `check:generated`: 1 of 14 stale (`content/docs/references/**`), fixed with `--fix`, then all 14 up to date.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations, one per refusal arm (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, on committed head 1ce3bc8342)</summary>

Anchor `  for (const fault of faults) {` (the default branch only, 1 hit) is replaced by a filter that drops one fault kind. Each mutation landed (anchor 1 to 0, blob 45cacf85f6f5 changed) and was restored to the HEAD blob 45cacf85f6f5 with `git diff HEAD` empty.

- not-a-field dropped: 5 failed (the no-`tenant_id` pin, the two opt-out pins, both door pins).
- non-text dropped: 6 failed (each non-text type pin).
- value-field dropped: 1 failed (the `valueFields` pin).

Controls stayed green in every leg.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Doors, measured. These refuse: `ObjectSchema.create()` and `defineStack()` (strict by default; `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID`), which throw when a code-authored stack's config module is evaluated; `os validate` (`validate.ts`, `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`), `os build` (= compile, the same schema), and the metadata save door, including the draft save that publish promotes (`resolveOverlaySchema` then `getMetadataTypeSchema('object')`, so 422). The publish promotion does not parse again. This does not refuse at boot: a stored `sys_metadata` row that fails the spec is "Registered anyway" with diagnostics (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`), and the sealer reports it as before. `registerObject` never parses.
- In-repo `lifecycle.seal` declarations with no `chainField`. Only the two spec fixtures above are refused, both case (a). Every plugin-audit and CLI fixture declares a text or lookup `tenant_id`, or registers raw. No shipped example, template, `create-objectstack` scaffold or hotcrm object declares `lifecycle.seal`.
- Skills readings. Lines (bytes, tokens):
  - `lifecycle.md` 199 to 199 (7721 to 7722 bytes; 1931 to 1931 tokens; ceiling 1931, headroom 0). The new teaching is paid for by deleting the old sentence.
  - `objects-fields-relationships.json` 438 to 438 (an eval fixture, not ratcheted).
  - Whole package, all SKILL.md: 4943 to 4943 lines. All of `skills/**`: 22762 to 22762 lines.
- False-refusal class, measured and accepted. The judgement reads the object's own declared fields plus the injected columns. An object whose `tenant_id` reaches it only through an `objectExtensions` entry is refused: `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse({ objects: [sealed], objectExtensions: [{ extend, fields: { tenant_id: text } }] })` fails at `objects.0.lifecycle.seal`, and the new door pin holds that. The sealer, which reads the folded field map, would seal such an object (read, not measured). The fix is to declare the column on the object; behaviour is unchanged.
- Accepted deviations (L2 N1, N3, left as they are): `lifecycle.md` says "no text `tenant_id`", although a lookup is accepted too (its own example uses one), because the token headroom is 0. The default message offers `organization_id` wherever the registry injects it, including where the author declared a non-text `organization_id` of their own.
- Known gap, not filed: a draft saved before this lands is promoted unjudged by publish. That holds for every `ObjectSchema` refinement.

## Verification

Files to read first: `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (`sealChainColumnFaults` and the default branch of `refuseUnknownSealChainField`; the risk is that the named messages must stay byte-identical), the new 34352 test file, and the changeset.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/object-lifecycle-seal-default-chain-column-34352.test.ts` should report 20 passed.

It seals r1 and r2 with `valueFields: ['payload', 'tenant_id']`, drops `tenant_id` from `valueFields`, then seals r3. The checkpoints read `org:org_a window r1`, `r2`, `r3`, with no re-seal; `verifyAuditLedger` reports no faults and `ok: true`, both whole and scoped to `org_a`. plugin-audit closure build plus that file under os-verify-lock: Test Files 1 passed, Tests 53 passed; VERDICT command-exit 0.
- N4: (b) now reads "some or all of its rows (every row whose value the driver returns as a non-string)", matching the spec docblock.
